acceptedChanges: The initial production OrdinaryAdmissionLease explicitly uses initiallyAdmitted=false. The test requires runIfAdmitted to return false and verifies its action did not execute. That initial lease is revoked and its dispatch worker joined.

prepareReplacement creates a fresh closed lease with the actual token and binding. publishReplacement checks those values, admits that lease and installs it. ordinaryAdmissionOpen now reads the production helper state.

acceptExchange captures admission under admissionLock at socket accept. The captured lease tracks the socket. Control ownership is released before reconnect handoff. Ordinary delivery uses that same lease.dispatch and runIfAdmitted; an initially unadmitted socket cannot acquire the later lease merely because its read finishes after publication.

Android now checks requiresAck=false and exact batteryLevel-only payload equality. A successful receive requires real authenticated delivery through the admitted helper. A failed dispatch submission leaves incoming incomplete, causing timeout rather than a false receive count.

finalAssessment: closeAdmissions captures distinct current/prepared/retiring leases under admissionLock, clears all references, revokes each lease, and awaits each dispatch worker outside the lock. It is safe to call again when the inventory is empty.

The successful path calls coordinator.closeAndAwait first, then closeAdmissions, closes the server, joins the receiver, and only then cancels scope and evaluates cleanupComplete. The former assertion-before-teardown ordering is gone.

The cleanup flag now follows completed lease joins as well as coordinator/server/receiver observations. The oracle write occurs only after check(passed). No lease count is hardcoded to make the assertion pass.

dispositions.assessment: Both peers retain the full authenticated endpoint record and require storedAfter.proofID equal to the actual successful diagnostics/result proofID. A requires no existing oracle. B and B-restart compare the existing previous-proof.sha256 to SHA-256(storedBefore.proofID) before starting a new proof. After local assertions succeed, each writes a new oracle from the fresh completed transcript.
dispositions.oracleLogic: The expected hash is retained from the prior phase rather than recomputed from the record being checked. Read-before-write ordering makes this an independent continuity assertion. A missing/mismatched oracle or authenticated record fails; so does a commit that silently retains the previous B proof while the endpoint stays unchanged. Oracle write errors prevent PASS.
limits: The oracle is test evidence, not production authorization or a secret key.
Android writeText has no atomic/fsync crash guarantee; Swift atomic write is not an explicit fsync durability test. The assertions support orderly process-restart continuity, not power-loss behavior.
The supervisor must establish actual process replacement and cross-phase proof uniqueness; a phase argument alone cannot prove restart.
No following phase reloads the final B-restart proof. Its immediate post-commit read is checked, but another process restart after B-restart is outside this sequence.
No prior encrypted frame is replayed, so durable receive replay rejection remains untested.

probeOrderingFollowup.causality: The contract permits phone-local completion after writing done, while Mac admission opens only after its initiator consumes and validates done. An immediate phone ordinary socket can therefore be accepted while the Mac generation remains closed. The listener captures admission at accept; later admission opening does not authorize that socket. A successful no-ack send is not proof that the peer consumed the event. This source-consistent explanation is the parent diagnosis, not an independently traced packet timeline.

verifiedTestChange.assessment: Android now awaits and validates the Mac device.status, including IDs, requiresAck=false and exact payload, before constructing/sending its one device.status response. Swift first completes the proof, opens real lifetime admission, sets the observer generation, and only then sends its probe. Thus this controlled exchange orders the phone response after Mac admission has opened.
